chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Salamah al-Lu'lu'i, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Shall I not inform you of how the Islam of Salman and Abu Dharr was?
So the man said, and he was hasty: 'As for the Islam of Salman, I have known it. Inform me of the Islam of Abu Dharr.'

He said: 'Indeed, Abu Dharr was in the valley of Mar, tending his sheep. A wolf came from the right of his sheep, so he struck the wolf with his staff. The wolf came from his left, so Abu Dharr struck it.'
Then Abu Dharr said to it, 'I have not seen a wolf more vicious than you, nor more evil.' The wolf said to him, 'More evil than I, by Allah, are the people of Mecca.'
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent a Prophet to them, but they belied him and insulted him.' This fell into the ears of Abu Dharr.
So he said to his wife, 'Bring me my provisions, my bag, and my staff.' Then he set out on foot, intending Mecca, to know the news of the wolf and what it had brought him.
Until he reached Mecca and entered it in a hot hour, having grown weary and exhausted. He came to Zamzam, being thirsty, so he scooped a bucket and it turned out to be milk.
So he said to himself, 'This, by Allah, indicates to me that what the wolf informed me of and what I have come for is true.' So he drank and came to a side of the Masjid.
There was a circle of Quraysh, so he sat with them. He saw them insulting the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), just as the wolf had said.
They did not cease in that, mentioning the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and insulting him, until Abu Talib came from the end of the day.
When they saw him, some of them said to others, 'Refrain, for his uncle has come.' So they refrained. He did not cease talking to them and speaking to them until it was the end of the day.
Then he stood up, and I rose following him. He turned to me and said, 'Mention your need.' I said, 'This is the Prophet sent among you.'
He said, 'And what do you do with him?' I said, 'I believe in him and affirm him, and I present myself to him, and he does not command me with anything except that I obey him.'
He said, 'And you will do that?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Come tomorrow at this time to me, until I take you to him.'
He said: 'I spent that night in the Masjid. When it was the next day, I sat with them. They did not cease mentioning the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and insulting him.'
Until Abu Talib appeared. When they saw him, some said to others, 'Hold back, for his uncle has come.' So they held back.
He did not cease talking to them until he stood up, so I followed him. I greeted him, so he said, 'Mention your need.'

I said, 'The Prophet sent among you.' He said, 'And what do you do with him?' I said, 'I believe in him and affirm him, and I present myself to him, and he does not command me with anything except that I obey him.'
He said, 'And you will do that?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Rise with me.' So I followed him, and he took me to a house in which was Hamza (peace be upon him).
I greeted him and sat down. He said to me, 'What is your need?' I said, 'This is the Prophet sent among you.'
He said, 'And what is your need to him?' I said, 'I believe in him and affirm him, and I present myself to him, and he does not command me with anything except that I obey him.'
He said, 'Do you testify that there is no god except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah?' I said, 'I testified.'
So Hamza took me to a house in which was Ja'far (peace be upon him). I greeted him and sat down.
Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me, 'What is your need?' I said, 'This is the Prophet sent among you.'
He said, 'And what is your need to him?' I said, 'I believe in him and affirm him, and I present myself to him, and he does not command me with anything except that I obey him.'
He said, 'Do you testify that there is no god except Allah, One, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger?' I said, 'I testified.'
He took me to a house in which was Ali (peace be upon him). I greeted him and sat down.
He said, 'What is your need?' I said, 'This is the Prophet sent among you.'
He said, 'And what is your need to him?' I said, 'I believe in him and affirm him, and I present myself to him, and he does not command me with anything except that I obey him.'
He said, 'Do you testify that there is no god except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah?' I said, 'I testified.'
He took me to a house in which was the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). I greeted him and sat down.
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to me, 'What is your need?' I said, 'The Prophet sent among you.'
He said, 'And what is your need to him?' I said, 'I believe in him and affirm him, and he does not command me with anything except that I obey him.'

He said, 'Do you testify that there is no god except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah?' I said, 'I testify that there is no god except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.'

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to me, 'O Abu Dharr! Go to your land, for you will find a cousin of yours who has died and has no heir except you. So take his wealth and stay with your family until our matter becomes apparent.'
So Abu Dharr returned, took the wealth, and stayed with his family until the matter of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) became apparent.
So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'This is the hadith of Abu Dharr and his Islam, may Allah be pleased with him.'
And as for the hadith of Salman, you have heard it.
He said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, narrate to me the hadith of Salman.'
'You have heard it.' And he did not narrate it to him due to his bad manners.

key_terms.أَبُو ذَرٍّ: Abu Dharr (a companion of the Prophet)
key_terms.أَمْرُنَا: Our matter (the public proclamation of Islam)

ai.seo_question: How did Abu Dharr al-Ghari convert to Islam according to Shia hadith sources?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the unique, miraculous nature of Abu Dharr’s early faith, where a speaking wolf serves as a divine sign prompting his journey to Mecca. It illustrates the gradual public revelation of Islam, as the Prophet instructs him to remain in his tribe until the 'matter becomes manifest,' reflecting the strategic patience of the early Meccan period. The narrative also subtly underscores the high scholarly etiquette, noting that Salman al-Farsi was excluded from hearing this specific account due to his brevity in transmission.
